title: Implement kernel selector v2 core logic (table-driven) w/ v1 fallback + deterministic tie-break
creator: Grace Kim
description:
Build the selector v2 core decision logic as a table-driven implementation.

Scope:
- Load + validate registry (versioned) into in-memory structures suitable for hot path selection.
- Implement SelectKernelV2(context) that chooses attention/prefill/decode kernels based on:
  (1) model family (+ key flags like GQA/MQA if present)
  (2) seq-length bucket / regime (prefill vs decode; short/medium/long context buckets)
  (3) normalized GPU SKU / capability bucket
- Deterministic tie-breaking when multiple candidates match.
- Safe fallback to v1 selector under any of:
  - unknown/partial model family metadata
  - missing registry entries
  - registry parse/validation errors (should fail closed to v1, not crash serving)
  - GPU SKU not recognized (should map to generic capability bucket if possible, else v1)
- Selector version tagging in decision output for telemetry (actual metrics implemented in ENG-3927, but selector must return selector_version + kernel_id).

Non-goals:
- Adding new kernels.
- Scheduler integration to supply seq bucket signals (ENG-3924), though selector API should accept these fields.

Notes:
- This ticket is intentionally focused on core selection mechanics and correctness guarantees (no perf tuning without data). Registry content will evolve via ENG-3926 + follow-up PRs for model families.
acceptance_criteria:
1) SelectorV2 chooses a kernel using the registry when an exact match exists for (model_family, seq_bucket, gpu_bucket).
2) SelectorV2 is deterministic: identical input context must always return identical kernel_id.
3) Tie-breaking rules are explicit and covered by tests (see below).
4) SelectorV2 falls back to v1 without crashing for unknown model families, missing entries, malformed registry rows, or unknown GPU bucket.
5) Unit tests cover:
   - exact match
   - fallback to wildcard rows
   - unknown model family -> v1
   - unknown gpu bucket -> capability fallback OR v1
   - multiple matches -> deterministic winner
   - registry validation: reject ambiguous rows where precedence cannot be resolved
6) Perf: no measurable overhead on the hot path beyond ~1–2% CPU in microbench (sanity check only; deeper perf in ENG-3929).
implementation_plan:
Implementation outline:
A) Interfaces
- Define SelectorContext:
  - model_id / model_family (string)
  - model_flags (e.g., gqa=true/false; may be unknown)
  - seq_bucket (enum: prefill_short/prefill_long/decode_short/decode_long; placeholder until ENG-3924 wires it)
  - gpu_bucket (enum/string from normalized SKU; placeholder until ENG-3925 lands)
  - selector_version_requested (v1|v2|auto) (v2 flag/override wiring is ENG-3931, but keep a hook)
- Define SelectionResult:
  - kernel_id
  - selector_version_used (v1|v2)
  - match_path (string enum: exact|wildcard|capability_fallback|v1_fallback) (for debugging + telemetry)

B) Registry loading
- Parse registry into rows keyed by (model_family, seq_bucket, gpu_bucket, optional flags).
- Validate on load:
  - required fields present
  - kernel_id exists in compiled-in kernel catalog
  - no duplicate rows with identical specificity
  - precedence rules produce a single winner for any given context
- On validation failure: log once at startup (or on reload), mark selector_v2_unavailable, and always return v1.

C) Matching + precedence
- Matching order (most-specific first):
  1) exact model_family + exact seq_bucket + exact gpu_bucket + exact relevant flags
  2) exact model_family + exact seq_bucket + exact gpu_bucket + flags wildcard
  3) exact model_family + exact seq_bucket + gpu wildcard ("any")
  4) exact model_family + seq wildcard + gpu wildcard
  5) family wildcard ("default") + ... (only if explicitly allowed)
- Deterministic tie-break:
  - compute specificity score = (# exact dims matched) + (# exact flag matches)
  - if scores tie, prefer row with higher "priority" field from registry (integer)
  - if still tie, choose lexicographically smallest kernel_id to ensure determinism across builds
  - if still tie (should not happen if validation is correct), treat as registry ambiguity -> v1 fallback + counter

D) Fallback behavior
- If context missing model_family or seq_bucket: v1
- If gpu bucket unknown but capability class known: map to capability bucket; attempt lookup; else v1
- Any runtime error in selection code path: catch + v1 (do not throw)

E) Tests
- Table-driven unit tests with a small fake registry and fake kernel catalog.
- Fuzz-ish test generating random rows and asserting deterministic output + no panics.

Open questions (track in comments):
- Whether to allow family wildcard rows at all, or keep v1 as the only true default.
- How to represent flags (GQA/MQA) in registry without exploding rows; likely treat missing flags as wildcard.
risk_notes:
Main risks:
- Incorrect precedence leading to unexpected kernel choice (perf regression) or illegal kernel for shape (correctness).
- Registry ambiguity causing non-determinism across deploys if not strictly validated.
- Overly aggressive wildcarding hiding missing coverage; we should prefer v1 fallback over guessing.

Mitigations:
- Strict registry validation with explicit precedence.
- Deterministic tie-breaker even in unexpected overlaps.
- Default behavior: v1 fallback unless a safe, explicit row matches.

comments: 2026-01-14 (Grace Kim): Kicking this off as the core selector implementation. Goal is to get a minimal but *strict* table-driven selector in place so we can iterate registry content separately. I’m planning to land behind an internal toggle but will keep the interface compatible with ENG-3931 wiring.

2026-01-16 (Noah Patel): Please make sure we never throw from hot path. If registry is bad, fail closed to v1 and emit a single-rate-limited log. Also recommend tie-break rule be independent of map iteration order (no hash-map ordering).

2026-01-20 (Yuki Sato): For unknown GPU SKUs: I’d prefer mapping to a capability class if we know SM + shared mem constraints. If we don’t know those, v1 fallback is fine. ENG-3925 will provide sku->bucket mapping; for now keep a placeholder hook.

2026-01-24 (Grace Kim): Drafted precedence rules in code + wrote unit tests around exact vs wildcard matches. Added explicit score + priority + lexicographic kernel_id as deterministic tie-break. Next: validation pass to reject ambiguous registry rows at load time.
2026-01-28 (Omar El-Sayed): Heads up: selector result needs to include selector_version_used for metrics. Even if telemetry ticket is separate, having the string in the result makes plumbing easier.

2026-02-02 (Grace Kim): Opened PR #18432. Includes: registry parser/validator, SelectKernelV2(), fallback to v1 on missing context, and deterministic tie-break. Left placeholders for seq_bucket + gpu_bucket until ENG-3924/3925 land. Added a microbench that exercises 1M selections; overhead looks negligible vs v1 on my dev box.

2026-02-05 (Hiro Tanaka): PR review: please tighten validation. If two rows match with same specificity and same priority, we should treat that as invalid registry (during load) rather than letting tie-break pick one silently. Determinism is good, but silent ambiguity makes future updates risky.

2026-02-07 (Grace Kim): Updated PR: registry load now fails validation if ambiguous rows could both win for any context given current precedence/priority rules. In that case selector v2 marks itself unavailable and returns v1 for all calls. Added tests that assert ambiguity causes fallback + an error counter increment (counter stubbed for ENG-3927).

2026-02-10 (Sana Farid): Please add a test that simulates partial metadata (model_family empty, or seq_bucket unknown) and asserts we *do not* attempt wildcard default rows. We don’t want accidental v2 enablement to change behavior when upstream hasn’t wired signals yet.

2026-02-12 (Grace Kim): Added partial-metadata tests and tightened behavior: missing model_family or missing seq_bucket -> unconditional v1. Also removed family wildcard support for now; design can revisit, but safer to require explicit family coverage.

2026-02-18 (Connor O'Brien): Release note: as long as this lands behind the v2 flag (ENG-3931), we can merge for runtime-1.19 train. Please coordinate with Benji on flag name + default state so we don’t accidentally enable on upgrade.
